judged_text: createEvent resolves the target calendar only via destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId) and silently falls back to primary, so review-base DestinationCalendar rows whose credentialId is NULL (the nullable legacy case every call site in this diff guards for) never match and their configured externalId is ignored. Bookings by hosts with legacy destination calendar rows are created on the Google account's primary calendar instead of the calendar the host configured (review-base used destinationCalendar.externalId), silently misdelivering events; because that credential-less fan-out path also writes references without externalCalendarId and the update/delete fallback is dead, those events can never be corrected or removed through Cal.com.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `createEvent` now selects `calendarId` only via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` and otherwise uses `"primary"`. In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, the legacy path for destinations with `destination.credentialId` falsy still calls `createEvent(c, event)` (no externalId passed) while `event.destinationCalendar` may contain entries whose `credentialId` is null. In that case, Google `createEvent` cannot match the configured destination calendar by `credentialId`, so it falls back to `primary`, ignoring the destination’s `externalId` (previous behavior used `destinationCalendar.externalId` directly). Also, `CalendarManager.createEvent` accepts `externalId?: string` but does not pass it into `calendar.createEvent` (it only returns it in the `EventResult`), so the reference will have `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` which is undefined for the legacy/fan-out path, reinforcing the mis-targeting.
